items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: you’ve got to learn this first before you get to where you are when you get to Coltrane and Miles and all those people”

ctx.x: Yeah. If you were able to tell some future jazz star a couple words about what they should know about their own business. Do you have any thoughts on that?

Well, today I would tell any youngsters starting out, the most important thing is to try to get some experience with older players or people who’ve been out there. Because what’s happening now is a lot of youngsters are coming into the business and they make the records and the records sold, and they’re hot records. But they don’t have any experience about playing with anybody, you know they don’t have the experience. And they don’t really have a style. For example, when I came along, you could recognize the…
I suppose it would depend on what their parents were listening to.

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Miles called me and said, “I’d like to have Cannonball. Is it okay with you?”

ctx.x: Into everything. I don’t know. His schedule – he was doing something all the time, and he was being called on for all kinds of different projects. A lot of projects that Cannon worked on, I was not a part of. I didn’t collect commissions on everything he did because we were a – when he went with Miles, for example, that was to me a key – a growing – because Miles called me and said, “I’d like to have Cannonball. Is it okay with you?” We talked about it. I didn’t want to – I didn’t get involved with any of the…
He was one of the influences that brought Nancy . . .
